video.title: I Asked 5 AI Tools to Make Me Rich. Then THIS Happened…

summary: Chris Koerner compares ChatGPT 5, Claude Opus 4.1, Grok 4 and Gemini 2.5 Pro on business-building prompts, then tests three models with real options trades. The models suggest several consulting offers, including paid ads, AI implementation, custom GPTs and no-code automation, but Koerner does not test those businesses with customers. He prefers Claude’s practical consultant plan and Gemini’s detailed automation plan, while criticizing Gemini’s length and ChatGPT’s brevity. In the trading segment, he reports a net $187 profit from three trades, while stressing that the result is a one-day sample and not investment advice.

ideas.offer: Learn basic campaign setup and optimization, then offer an ad setup or optimization service.

Grok recommends door-to-door outreach and supplies a script. This requires a person in the field.

ideas.delivery: The founder would learn basic Facebook and Google campaign setup, then set up or optimize ads for a client. Grok suggests Google Skillshop, Facebook Blueprint and tutorials as learning resources; delivery was not tested.

acquisition.how: A software agent could build a prospect list, but the described door-to-door selling is in person and needs a human. Any digital outreach would need to follow UK marketing rules.

onboarding.how: Forms and scheduling could collect account details, but a human would need to confirm access, budget and goals.

delivery.how: Software can help with campaign setup and reporting, but planning and optimizing ads for a client's business need human review.

billing.how: Invoicing and recurring payment collection could be automated after the service and billing terms are set.

support.how: Agents could answer routine questions from campaign reports, but a human should handle budget and performance decisions.

uk_applicability.notes: The service and ad platforms can be used in the UK, with local market and campaign adjustments. Door-to-door sales still require a person; UK marketing outreach must follow PECR and call-screening rules.

risks: The plan's learning and closing timeline is ambitious and no paying client or campaign result is demonstrated.
The proposed outreach volume and scripts do not establish that prospects will convert.
In the UK, unsolicited marketing messages to individuals and sole traders require consent; cold email to limited companies is allowed, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.

tactics.name: Compare model outputs with consistent criteria
steps: Give each model the same prompt and relevant context.
Compare usefulness, clarity, likely feasibility and answer length.

warnings.warning: The host says the options data from Gemini was outdated and its first suggested QQQ strike was not viable at the current price.
The host had little options-trading experience, placed real trades based on model suggestions and notes that options can expire worthless.
The host says the trading result is from a sample of one day, tells viewers to do their own research and says it is not investment advice.
The host questions whether small businesses need custom GPTs and whether coffee shops would pay for one.
Claude's plan suggests fictional but realistic case studies. Do not present fictional examples as real client work.
AI-generated consulting prices, market-size claims and outreach targets are not verified sales data; no consulting business was tested in the video.

For UK acquisition, unsolicited marketing SMS, WhatsApp, DMs and emails to individuals and sole traders require consent under PECR; cold email to limited companies is allowed, and cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.
The host promotes his own TK Owners community and TKOPod newsletter and podcast; he says he has no affiliate links and is not sponsored by the AI companies.

lessons.lesson: Give a model relevant context about your skills, constraints and preferences, and ask it to clarify before recommending a plan.

quote.text: Ask it to ask you the right questions that it needs to get the most context that it needs to give you the best output.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A detailed prompt can produce more actionable steps, but a longer answer is not automatically better.

quote.text: Okay, more does not always equal better, but I'm going to call it quality density.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Start customer outreach early instead of spending the whole launch window learning and preparing.

quote.text: Claude wants me to start doing outreach on day one, which I love.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A small project that fixes one clear, painful task can be an easier first sale than a broad transformation proposal.

quote.text: The initial offer will focus on solving one specific, highly painful, and easily automated task for the client.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Explain the value in customer terms such as time and money saved, and avoid promising results that have not been demonstrated.

quote.text: Don't overpromise. Don't talk tech. Talk time and money saved.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use real demonstrations, testimonials and documented client results to build credibility.

quote.text: The beta tester play is offer three businesses free setup in exchange for video testimonials.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Do not assume that a new technology is a must-have for every small business; test whether a specific customer will pay for it.

quote.text: I don't know if a coffee shop needs their own GPT. Maybe in the future that'll be a thing, but I feel like that's like saying 15 years ago, every coffee shop's going to have their own app.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Check live, primary information before acting on an AI response when prices or conditions can change quickly.

quote.text: The price was outdated. It was using an outdated price because the current share price is 5.56.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Confident AI explanations do not remove the need to understand the downside of a decision.

quote.text: If QQQ shares aren't 564 or lower on August 8th, this option will expire worthless.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Treat a one-day investment result as a single observation, not proof that a strategy works.

quote.text: So, sample size of one day, results not guaranteed. Do your own research.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: The consulting ideas and their prices, customer counts and timelines are AI-generated recommendations that the host did not test with customers. The options trades and outcomes are presented as first-hand, but cover one day and include an acknowledged stale-price error and conflicting trade-cost figures.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host promotes his TK Owners community and TKOPod newsletter and podcast. He says he has no affiliate links and is not sponsored by the AI companies.
